page: Amazon Web Services d3.2xlarge is a dense storage instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor running at 3.1 GHz, delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core.

A defining characteristic of the d3.2xlarge is its massive local storage capacity, offering 11,880 GB of local HDD storage. This dense storage configuration is paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. No dedicated GPUs are included in this instance configuration.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, scoring in the bottom 25% on stress-ng and Geekbench tests. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the average range, representing the middle 50% of tested servers. This highlights a tradeoff where raw single-threaded compute is limited, but the instance maintains stable multi-threaded throughput and memory performance.

Given the massive HDD capacity and average multi-core performance, the d3.2xlarge is highly cost-efficient for storage-intensive workloads that do not require high-speed SSD IOPS. It is well-suited for large-scale data warehousing, MapReduce jobs, distributed file systems, and big data analytics where sequential disk throughput and high resource density are prioritized over raw compute speed.
